hook.alt: An old map of Florida split into East Florida and West Florida
hook.cap: East and West Florida, printed in London in 1763. Library of Congress.
hook.note: I'm stuck in Canvas, so I can't go anywhere. In 1763 Britain took Florida. What did a British town look like?

opti.brief: She can't leave Canvas, so you go. Scout a British town in VR and send her one short video.
opti.desk: No headset? Use my desk. Put each card on the timeline, then write 2 sentences.

vr.look: A colony is land ruled by a faraway country. Britain ruled this town, Williamsburg, Virginia. From 1763 to 1783, Britain ruled Florida too.

place.alt: An old hand-drawn map with a marsh, a road and a small square fort
place.html: In 1763: new rulers, new laws. Most Spanish families, and the people of Fort Mose, left for Cuba.
place.cap: Fort Mose on a British map, 1760s. Library of Congress.

say: When Florida changed hands in 1763, ___ changed for the people.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
@PLACE@

In your video, you say these 2 sentences:

@SAY@

Practice now. Say both before the timer ends.

@TIMER@

In VR, this page is on the Canvas tab.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Williamsburg in Filter environments. Click Colonial Williamsburg, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Scout the town
steps.html: Move with the thumbstick. Walk down the main street. Stop where you can see many houses.

steps.title: Record your video and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Fit the street in the tablet. Click Record video, say your 2 sentences, and click it again to stop.

On the Canvas tab, pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your video, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 To fix it, send a new video.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your video is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? See Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Turn slowly while you record, so your teacher can see the whole street.

vr.full: One video, 30 seconds or less, showing the place while you say both sentences.

studio.title: Who ruled Florida?
studio.look: A timeline shows events in order. Each part shows who ruled Florida then. Each card is an event from our lessons.
studio.do: Read the date. Tap where it fits, or drag the card there.

game.miss: Not that part. Read the date on the card, then check the timeline again.
game.done: Done! Florida changed hands three times. Each time, the rules changed for the people here.

cards.name: Fort Mose begins
cards.what: The first free Black town the law allowed.
cards.alt: An old map with a small fort by a marsh
cards.ok: Yes! Spanish Florida set up Fort Mose in 1738.

cards.name: Florida is split in two
cards.alt: An old map of East and West Florida
cards.ok: Yes! Britain split Florida in two in 1763.

cards.name: St. Augustine is built
cards.what: Spain builds a town on the Atlantic coast.
cards.ok: Yes! Spain built St. Augustine in 1565.

cards.name: American settlers move in
cards.ok: Yes! Spain's second turn was weaker, and settlers moved in.

cards.name: Plantations grow
cards.what: New settlers come, and slavery spreads.
cards.ok: Yes. Under British rule, plantations grew and slavery spread.

cards.name: Florida becomes a U.S. territory
cards.ok: Yes! In 1821 Florida became land owned by the United States.
